44. The Lord said to my Lord. Here the Holy Spirit puts into the mouth of all the godly a song of triumph, that they may boldly defy Satan and all the ungodly, and mock at their rage, when they endeavor to drive Christ from his throne. That they may not hesitate or tremble, when they perceive great emotions produced in the earth, they are commanded to place the holy and inviolable decree of God in opposition to all the exertions of adversaries. The meaning therefore is: whatever may be the madness of men, all that they shall dare to contrive will be of no avail for destroying the kingdom of Christ, which has been set up, not by the will of men, but by the appointment of God, and therefore is supported by everlasting strength. Whenever this kingdom is violently attacked, let us call to remembrance this revelation from heaven; for undoubtedly this promise was put into the hand of Christ, that every believer may apply it to his own use. But God never changes or deceives, so as to retract what has once gone out of his mouth.
Sit at my right hand. This phrase is used metaphorically for the second or next rank, which is occupied by God’s deputy. And therefore it signifies, to hold the highest government and power in the name of God, as we know that God has committed his authority to his only-begotten Son, so as to govern his Church by his agency. This mode of expression, therefore, does not denote any particular place, but, on the contrary, embraces heaven and earth under the government of Christ. And God declares that Christ will sit till his enemies be subdued, in order to inform us that his kingdom will remain invincible against every attack; not that, when his enemies have been subdued, he will be deprived of the power which had been granted to him, but that, while the whole multitude of his enemies shall be laid low, his power will remain for ever unimpaired. In the meantime, it points out that condition of his kingdom which we perceive in the present day, that we may not be uneasy when we see it attacked on all sides.
MATTHEW 23:1-12; MARK 12:38-39; LUKE 11:43, 45-46; 20:45-46
Matthew 23:1-12
Mark 12:38-39
Luke 11:45-46
1. Then Jesus spoke to the multitude, and to his disciples, 2. Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in the chair of Moses. 3. Observe and do, therefore, all things whatever they command you to observe; but do not according to their works; for they say and do not. 4. For they bind heavy and intolerable burdens, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they refuse to touch them with their finger. 5. And they do all their works that they may be seen by men, and make their phylacteries broad, and wear large fringes on their robes, 6. And love the first places at entertainments, and the first seats in the synagogues, 7. And salutations in the marketplace, and to be called by men Rabbi.
“Estre appelez des hommes Maistres;” — “to be called by men Masters.”
8. But as for you, be not called Rabbi;
“No Soyez point appelez Maistres;” — “but not be called Masters.”
for there is one who is your Master, Christ; and you are all brethren. 9. And do not call any one on earth your Father; for one is your Father, who is in heaven. 10. And be not called Masters;
“Docteurs;” — “doctors.”
for one is your Master, Christ. 11. He who is greatest among you shall be your servant. 12. But he that exalteth himself shall be humbled; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
38. And he said to them in his doctrine, Beware of the scribes, who love to walk in robes, and love salutations in the marketplaces, 39. And the first seats in the synagogues, and the first places at entertainments.
45. And one of the lawyers
“Un des docteurs de la loy;” — “one of the doctors of the law.”
answering said to him, Master, in saying these things thou also reproachest us. 46. And he said, Woe also to you, lawyers! for you load men with burdens which are intolerable; and you yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers. (A little before.)
Luke 20:45-46
45. And while all the people were hearing, he said to his disciples, 46. Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in robes, and love salutations in the marketplaces and the first seats in the synagogues, and the first places at entertainments.

entries.0ab01ee4c70a847022fbee805fcb45edf8e2565c:
<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22" type="chapter">
               <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:259" />
               <ns0:head>CHAP. XXII.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 ANd Jesus answered, <ns0:note place="margin">Luke 14.6.</ns0:note> and spake again to them by parables, and said:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 The kingdom of heaven, is like unto a cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain king, which made a marriage for his Son.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And sent forth his servants, to call them that were bidden to the wedding, and they would not come.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 Again, he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them which are bidden, Behold! I have prepared my dinner, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 9.2.</ns0:note> my oxen, and <ns0:hi>my</ns0:hi> fat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lings <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> killed, and all things <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> ready, come to the marriage.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 But they made light of <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dise.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 And the remnant took his servants, and intreated <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> spitefully, and slew <ns0:hi>them.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 But when the king heard <ns0:hi>thereof,</ns0:hi> he was wroth, and he sent forth his armies, and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroyed those murderers, and burnt up their city.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden, were not worthy.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Go ye therefore into the high-ways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />age.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 So those servants went into the <ns0:hi>high</ns0:hi>-ways, and gathered together all, as many as they found both bad, and good, and the wedding was furnish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed with guests.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Cor. 5.3. Eph. 4.24. Col. 3.10.12. Rev. 3.4. & 16.15. & 19.8.</ns0:note> which had not on a wedding garment.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And he saith unto him, Friend! how cam<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est thou in hither, not having a wedding garment? And he wasspeechless.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Then said the king to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.12.</ns0:note> into outer darkness, there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 20.16.</ns0:note> For many are called, but few <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> cho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sen.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath this Parable, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14. from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. to 26. which hath made Diverse Interpreters think, that <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> hath put it out of its due order, for <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> reports it as spoken long be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore, and that not in the Temple, but at a <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> House where he was at Dinner, and upon occasion of one of them saying, <ns0:hi>Blessed is he that shall Eat Bread in the Kingdom of God.</ns0:hi> But I know no reason why we may not allow our Saviour to have used the same <ns0:hi>Parable</ns0:hi> twice, in two differing Companies, and upon two different occasions, especially con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sidering there are remarkable differences in <ns0:hi>Lukes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thews</ns0:hi> Relation. I shall therefore leave the consideration of <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi>'s Relation, till I come to that Chapter in his Gospel, where I shall meet with it in Course, and consider only what <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith. We must remember this is a <ns0:hi>Parable,</ns0:hi> not an Historical <ns0:hi>Narration.</ns0:hi> The first Verse tells us, <ns0:hi>Then Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sus answered,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>spake again to them in Parables,</ns0:hi> he an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swered, that is, He began a Discourse (so the Word very of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten signifies) our Saviour hath neither given us any particular Explication of this <ns0:hi>Parable,</ns0:hi> nor any <ns0:hi>Proparabola</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Epipa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rabola,</ns0:hi> any Sentence, before, or after the Parable, guiding us as to the Explication, except only that short Sentence, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:hi>For many are called but few are chosen,</ns0:hi> which rather guid<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth us in the Explication of the four latter Verses, than of the whole Parable, yet it is not hard for us to find out our Saviours Scope in this Parable. It seemeth to be double. 1. To inform those to whom he spake of the Destruction suddenly coming upon the Jews, for their Rejection of the Gospel, and of the calling of the Gentiles. To let us know that neither a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst the Jews nor Gentiles, all should be saved, whom God called by the External Ministration of the Gospel: But those alone who belonging to the Election of Grace, should be found in the Day of Judgment, having on the Wedding Gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment. So then: The <ns0:hi>Kingdom of Heaven</ns0:hi> here signifies, The way, or Equity of God in the Dispensation of the Gospel, or the Administration of things in order to the Kingdom of Glory. The <ns0:hi>King here</ns0:hi> mentioned, must be he who is <ns0:hi>the King of Kings.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Marriage for his Son,</ns0:hi> is the <ns0:hi>Exhibi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of the Covenant of Grace.</ns0:hi> Which whosoever layeth hold on, <ns0:hi>Isai.</ns0:hi> 56.4. is by Faith United to Christ, which <ns0:hi>Vnion</ns0:hi> is often expressed in Holy Writ, under the Notion of a <ns0:hi>Mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riage, Psal</ns0:hi> 45.10, 11. <ns0:hi>Ephe.</ns0:hi> 5.23, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Or their <ns0:hi>Vnion with him in Glory, Rev.</ns0:hi> 19.9. The Persons <ns0:hi>bidden</ns0:hi> were the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Servants</ns0:hi> that called them to the <ns0:hi>Wedding,</ns0:hi> were those that were faithful, amongst their ordinary Teachers, or the <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> such as <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> and the rest, whom they refused to hearken unto. The <ns0:hi>other Servants</ns0:hi> might signifie <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> and the twelve, and others sent out by Christ, to tell them that Christ was now come, there wanted nothing but their coming to him, and receiving of him. Their <ns0:hi>making Light of it, going one to his Farm, another to his Merchan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dise,</ns0:hi> and others <ns0:hi>taking the Servants, entreating the Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vants spitefully, and slaying them,</ns0:hi> signifies the Jews general refusal of the Gospel, and the particular Rage, and Malice of some of them, shewn in their abusing of the Lords <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> and Messengers, and which he knew some of them would further shew against <ns0:hi>Stephen</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iames.</ns0:hi> The Kings send<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing forth his Armies, and slaying the Murderers, signifyed the coming of the <ns0:hi>Roman Armies,</ns0:hi> and their utter destroying <ns0:hi>Ierusalem.</ns0:hi> The sending of the Servants into the High-ways, and inviting all those whom they found to the <ns0:hi>Wedding,</ns0:hi> sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nified the <ns0:hi>Apostles,</ns0:hi> going to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Preaching</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Gospel to all Nations.</ns0:hi> Which much inlarged the Territo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ries of the Church, gathering in many who professed to ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cept of Christ, but not all in Truth, and Sincerity. <ns0:hi>The Kings coming to see his Guests,</ns0:hi> signifyeth Christs com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing at the Day of the last Judgment, <ns0:hi>with his Fan in his Hand, throughly to purge his Floor.</ns0:hi> His finding <ns0:hi>one with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Wedding Garment,</ns0:hi> Signifyeth his finding many Hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrites at the Day of Judgment. The Guests at Weddings were either wont to put on their best Cloths (as we usually do) or a particular Garment which was then in use, and was worn by them, who were invited to Weddings. By the <ns0:hi>Wedding Garment here</ns0:hi> is meant <ns0:hi>Christ, Rom.</ns0:hi> 13.14. who is at this Feast, both the <ns0:hi>Bridegroom,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Meat at the Feast,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Wedding Garment</ns0:hi> also, in Diverse Respects. It is but an Idle Dispute, whether <ns0:hi>Faith is meant,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Love,</ns0:hi> neither the one nor the other seperately, but <ns0:hi>Faith that work<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth by Love.</ns0:hi> Whatsoever God requireth of us, that we may be made meet for the Kingdom of God, <ns0:hi>without Faith and Holiness none can see God.</ns0:hi> His being Speechless signifies, That those who have lived under the proffers of Grace and Salva<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, and have rejected them, neither believing in the Lord Jesus Christ, nor bringing forth Fruits of Holiness, will be <ns0:hi>without excuse at the Day of Iudgment.</ns0:hi> And the Kings Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manding <ns0:hi>his Servants to Bind him Hand and Foot,</ns0:hi> &c, sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifyeth that all such Persons as live within the Church, under the means of Grace, yet dye impenitent, and unbelievers, having not by a true Faith received Christ as their Saviour, and brought forth the Fruits of true Repentance and Holiness, shall get nothing by their being within the Church, and External<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly called, but shall be thrown to Hell as well as others, the pains of which are here expressed by <ns0:hi>Binding Hand and Foot</ns0:hi>; lying in <ns0:hi>outer Darkness, Weeping</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gnashing of Teeth,</ns0:hi> as in other places by a <ns0:hi>Worm that shall never dye,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Fire that shall never go out,</ns0:hi> all Metaphorical Expressions signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fying the Vexations, and Intolerable Punishment of the Damned in Hell. <ns0:hi>For</ns0:hi> (saith our Saviour) <ns0:hi>many are called, but few are chosen.</ns0:hi> We met with this Expression before, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 20.16. where the Sense of it was not so obvious, as it is here. Some by it here understood, a <ns0:hi>choice unto Life Eternal</ns0:hi>: Nor without reason, if that be understood, by the <ns0:hi>Marriage Supper,</ns0:hi> as it is <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 19.9. and it appears to be partly at least the Sense of it here, in that the Person without the Wedding Garment is Doomed to Eternal Misery: If we by the <ns0:hi>Mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riage</ns0:hi> Supper understand an <ns0:hi>Vnion with Christ here,</ns0:hi> or the Benefits flowing from that, we must by <ns0:hi>Chosen</ns0:hi> here under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand <ns0:hi>Effectually-called,</ns0:hi> being made partakers of that speci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />al, Distinguishing Grace, which bringeth Salvation. The Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel is Preached to many, whom God doth not favour with his <ns0:hi>special Grace,</ns0:hi> so as they receive it, convert and are saved. The former part of this Parable, doth hint us the reason why the Jews rejected the offers of Grace and Salvation made to them, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> The power that the Temptations from the World of Pleasure, Profit, and Honour had upon them. As the latter part also sheweth us the true reason why any are saved, to be <ns0:hi>from the free Grace of God, viz.</ns0:hi> because they are <ns0:hi>Chosen,</ns0:hi> chosen to Eternal Life, and particularly favoured to be made partakers of his special, and distinguish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Grace.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might entangle him in <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> talk.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark Ch.</ns0:hi> 12, 13. saith, <ns0:hi>They sent unto him certain of</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> and of the <ns0:hi>Herodians, to catch him in his Words. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 20.20. <ns0:hi>They watched him, and sent forth Spies, which should feign themselves just Men, that they might take hold of his Words, that so they might deliver him to the Power and Authority of the Governour.</ns0:hi> His Life was what they sought for. This they had no Power al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed by the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> to take away without the Sentence of <ns0:hi>Pontius Pilate,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Governour. That they might have something to accuse him of before him, which he might condemn him for, they first take Councel. They saw he did nothing worthy of <ns0:hi>Death:</ns0:hi> They therefore issue their Councels in a resolution, to send some Persons to discourse with him, un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der the pretence of Conscientious good Men, to propound some Questions to him, his Answer to which, might give them some opportunity to accuse him of <ns0:hi>Blasphemy,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Sedition.</ns0:hi> The men they pitch upon, were some of them <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> some <ns0:hi>Herodians.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:259" />16 And they sent out unto him their discip<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>es with the Herodians, saying, Master, We know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest thou for any man, for thou regardest not the person of men.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.14. So hath <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 20. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21. There is a great Variety of Opinions, who these <ns0:hi>He<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rodians were,</ns0:hi> we read of them in an early Consultation against <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> with the <ns0:hi>Pharisees, Mar.</ns0:hi> 3.6. Some think, they were Forreigners of other Nations; whom <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> being <ns0:hi>Tetrarch</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> had brought in from contiguous <ns0:hi>Pagan</ns0:hi> Nations, but this is not Probable, for then the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> would have had nothing to do with them. Others think, that they were some of <ns0:hi>Herods Guard,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Soldiers</ns0:hi>; but nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther is this Probable, considering the issue of their Councels, to send some whom Christ should not know, nor be frighted with. Others (which is more Probable) think they were <ns0:hi>some of those Iews, who favoured Herods</ns0:hi> side, and had for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gotten the Liberty of their Country, joyning with the Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />queror, and taking his Part. Others think they were <ns0:hi>Sad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duces.</ns0:hi> Others say, that they were Persons, that were of a Mungrel Religion, made up of <ns0:hi>Iudaism</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentilism. Mar.</ns0:hi> 8.15. Our Saviour bids them beware of the <ns0:hi>Leaven</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> and of <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi>; which maketh it Probable, That the <ns0:hi>Herodians</ns0:hi> were not only <ns0:hi>Courtiers,</ns0:hi> and for the <ns0:hi>Roman interest,</ns0:hi> but that they had imbraced some particular <ns0:hi>Doctrines,</ns0:hi> much differing from the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi>; it is likely, they were Leavened with some of the <ns0:hi>Doctrine</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Sad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duces,</ns0:hi> denying <ns0:hi>Angels</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Spirits,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Resurrection.</ns0:hi> It is plain, that they were some of <ns0:hi>Herods Faction,</ns0:hi> what their Principles were as to Religion, is not so plain, nor of much concern to us to know. They begin their Discourse to our Saviour, with a great Complement, <ns0:hi>Master,</ns0:hi> a Name the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> did usually give to those, whom they owned for Teachers. <ns0:hi>We know that thou art true,</ns0:hi> one that will tell us the Truth, and speak as thou thinkest to be true: <ns0:hi>And teachest the way of God in Truth, neither carest thou for any Man, for thou regardest not the Person of Men.</ns0:hi> Thou wilt speak nothing, out of Fear, nor for any Favour or Affection: But plainly tell us what is Truth, and what God would have us do, in the Cases we offer to thee. In these Words they give us the true Character of a good Teacher, he must be a good Man, True, one that will truly teach Men the way of God, and in the faithful discharge of their Duty, not be afraid of the Face of Men. But herein they condemned themselves, for if our Saviour was so, why did they not believe in him, and obey what he taught them? <ns0:hi>Tell us therefore what thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give Tribute unto Cesar? Or not?</ns0:hi> But how came this to be a Case of Conscience? What doubt could there be, whether Men for their Peace, might not lawfully part from their own, especially such a little part of it? Some think, that they spake with Relation to that particular Tribute, which was demanded, which they think, was that <ns0:hi>half Shekel, Exod.</ns0:hi> 30.12.15. paid by the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> every year, which was to go for the Service of the <ns0:hi>Tabernacle:</ns0:hi> They say, that the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> had ordered this <ns0:hi>Payment</ns0:hi> to go to the <ns0:hi>Emperor,</ns0:hi> and this bred the <ns0:hi>Question,</ns0:hi> Whether they might lawfully pay that which was appointed, as a Testimony of their Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mage to God, and for the Service of the Temple, to a profane use. I must confess I cannot so freely agree to this, wanting any good proof, that the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> exacted that Pay<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment for the <ns0:hi>Emperor,</ns0:hi> and thinking it a very probable Ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gument to the contrary, That the Tables of the <ns0:hi>Money-Changers,</ns0:hi> who changed the Peoples Money into half Shekels fit for that Payment, was now continued. And if that Pay<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment had been now altered, and turned to the use of the <ns0:hi>Civil Government,</ns0:hi> our Saviour's overturning those Tables and driving the Money Changers out, had offered them a fair opportunity, to have charged him with <ns0:hi>Sedition,</ns0:hi> which they did not do upon that Account. I rather therefore think the Question propounded concerning the Lawfulness of making any Payments to the <ns0:hi>Emperor,</ns0:hi> looking upon him, as an Usurper of Authority, over a <ns0:hi>free People.</ns0:hi> That the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were very tenacious of their Liberty, appears from <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 8.33. And without doubt, the most of them paid such Taxes, as the <ns0:hi>Roman Emperor</ns0:hi> laid upon them, with no very Good Will. Now these Hypocrites turn it into a <ns0:hi>Case of Conscience</ns0:hi>; God having made the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> a free People, whether they should not sin against God, in paying these Civil Taxes to a <ns0:hi>Pagan Conqueror?</ns0:hi> There was one <ns0:hi>Theudas,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 5.36, 37. who made an Insurrection upon it. This was a Question Captio<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s enough. For if he had said it was <ns0:hi>Law<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful,</ns0:hi> he had probably incurred the <ns0:hi>Odium</ns0:hi> of the People, which was what they desired, for they had apprehended him before this time, but for Fear of them. If he had said, <ns0:hi>It is not Lawful,</ns0:hi> they had what they sought for, a fair opportu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nity for accusing him, and delivering him up to <ns0:hi>Pontius Pilate,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Roman Governour</ns0:hi> at this time amongst them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Shew me the tribute money. And <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>See</ns0:hi> Chap 20.2.</ns0:note> they brought to him a <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>In value Se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven pence Half-peny.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> peny.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And he saith unto them, Whose <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> this image, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Inscrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> superscription?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 They say unto him Cesars. Then saith he unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 17.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Rom. 13.7.</ns0:note> Render therefore unto Cesar, the things that are Cesars, and unto God, the things that are Gods.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 When they had heard <ns0:hi>these words,</ns0:hi> they mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />velled, and left him, and went their way.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.15, 16, 17. So hath <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 20.23, 24, 25, 26. Our Saviour, saith <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> perceived their <ns0:hi>Craftiness,</ns0:hi> how subtilly they went about to entrap him. He calls them to shew him the <ns0:hi>Tribute Money:</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had two sorts of Money: <ns0:hi>Shekels</ns0:hi> and half <ns0:hi>Shekels,</ns0:hi> which was Money proper to them, and <ns0:hi>Roman Coin, Pence</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sesterces.</ns0:hi> Their Tribute was paid in this <ns0:hi>Coin.</ns0:hi> Accordingly they bring unto him a <ns0:hi>Penny,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Penny as much in value as se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven Pence half Peny in our Coin: Which it seems was the <ns0:hi>Poll-money,</ns0:hi> which the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> exacted of every Head. The Coining of Money was always lookt upon, as an Act of So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veraign Power, hence the Usurpation of it is made so Cri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />minal: Most Princes use to have their Effigies stampt upon their Coin, and some Inscription about it, with their Names, and some Words expressive of their Dominion over such places, where their Coin is Currant: So as the admission of a Princes Coin as Currant amongst a People, was a Testimony of their owning, and subjection to such a Prince. Such an Image and Superscription this piece of Money had: Upon which our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour concludes, <ns0:hi>Render therefore unto Cesar, the things which are Cesars, and unto God, the things that are Gods.</ns0:hi> Altho <ns0:hi>Cesar</ns0:hi> be an Usurper, yet God hath given you into his Hands, you have owned him, by accepting his Coin, as Cur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rant amongst you. His right, and Gods right are two distinct things. Religion doth not exempt you from your Civil Duties, and Obedience to Princes, in things wherein they have a Power to Command. Princes have Power to impose Tributes upon their Subjects, for the Maintenance, and upholding of the Civil Government. Let <ns0:hi>Cesar</ns0:hi> have his due, and let God have his right: You are a Company of Hypocrites, who by this Que<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />steion would make me believe you have a great Zeal for God, and his Rights; and that you would not pay Taxes, that you might assert Gods Right over you, this is your Pretence; but indeed your Design is to try me, if you can perswade me by any Words of mine, to incourage you to any Sedition, or Acts of Disloyalty to your Civil Governors. I see no reason for it, <ns0:hi>Cesar</ns0:hi> hath his Right, and God hath his Rights, you may give them both their Rights, and so you ought to do. Gods Kingdom is of another Nature, than the Kingdoms of the World. His Law forbiddeth no <ns0:hi>Civil Rights.</ns0:hi> Thus our Saviour Answers their Question so, as he maketh them to condemn themselves, if owning the Civil Magistrates Power, they did not give him his Rights, and so, as neither <ns0:hi>Cesar,</ns0:hi> nor yet the People had any just Cause of Exception against him for his Words. This Answer surprizeth them, they mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vel, and go their way, having plaid their Game, and got no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 The same day came to him the Sadduces, which say that there is no resurrection & asked him,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man dye having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Now there was with us seven brethren, and the first, when he had married a wife, de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceased, and having no issue, left his wife unto his brother.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Likewise the second also, and the third, unto the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 paragraph">
                        <ns0:desc>〈1 paragraph〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> seventh.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And last of all the woman dyed also.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> thus repeats the same History, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.18, 19, 20. &c. So doth <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 20.27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33. Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning the <ns0:hi>Sadduces,</ns0:hi> we have before spoken, they were a Sect amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> much differing from the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> as may be seen, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 23.8. Amongst other Erroneous <ns0:hi>Tenets,</ns0:hi> they denied the <ns0:hi>Resurrection,</ns0:hi> as may be seen in the Text, as well as this; and (which indeed was their Fundamental <ns0:hi>Error</ns0:hi>) they denied <ns0:hi>Spirits,</ns0:hi> and consequently the immortality of the Soul in its separate Estate. Their design seemeth not so much to have been, to have drawn out a Discourse from our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />our; which might have touched his Life, (which was the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> de<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ign) as to have exposed him, by bringing him to an absurdity. To this purpose they p<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t a Case to our Saviour upon the Law, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 25.5. where God had ordained, for the Preservation of the Inheritances, of the several Tribes and Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />milies di<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tinct, <ns0:hi>That if Brethren dwell together, and one of them died leaving no issue, the Wife of the dead should not M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>rry unto a stranger, her Husbands Brother should go in unto her, and take her to him to W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>fe,</ns0:hi> &c. Now they either knew of, or else supposed a Case of seven Brethren, succe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sively Marrying the same Woman; they desire to know, whose Wife of the seven this Woman should be in the <ns0:hi>Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection</ns0:hi>? Instead of D<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>scovering their acuteness, and putting our Saviour upon a Difficulty, they did but betray their own Ignorance, as to the state of the Resurrection.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:260" />29 Jesus answered, and said unto them, Ye do err not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 For in the resurrection, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Joh. 3.2.</ns0:note> are as the an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gels of God in heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.24, 25. only he propounds it as a Question: <ns0:hi>Do ye not therefore err, because you know not the Scriptures? Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 20.34, 35. <ns0:hi>And Iesus answering, said unto them, The Children of this World Marry, and are given in Marriage: But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that World, and the Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection of the Dead, neither Marry, nor are given in Mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riage. Neither can they dye any more, for they are equal to the Angels, and are the Children of God, being the Chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren of the Resurrection.</ns0:hi> The Discourse of the <ns0:hi>Sadduces</ns0:hi> was bottomed upon this mistake, That there should not only be a Resurrection of Bodies, but of Relations too; and the state of the World to come, should be like the state of this World, in which for the Propagation and Continuance of mankind, Men and Women marry, and are given in Mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riage. Now saith our Saviour, Your Error is bottomed in your Ignorance, because you know not the Scriptures, (which indeed is the Foundation of all Mens Errors, in matter of Faith,) nor <ns0:hi>the Power of God.</ns0:hi> If you knew the Power of God, you would know, that God is able to raise the Dead; to confirm our Faith in the Resurrection; the Scripture every where sendeth us to the Consideration of the <ns0:hi>Divine Power. Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.11. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 3.21. If you knew the Scriptures, you would know that God will raise the Dead, and the state of Men in the Resurrection shall not be as in this Life, where Men and Women dye, Daily; and in Case they did not Marry, and give in Marriage, the Generation of Men would quickly be extinct. But (saith <ns0:hi>Luke) They who shall be accounted worthy to obtain that World,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>the Resurrection from the Dead.</ns0:hi> It is manifest by the first Words, that the latter Words are not to be understood of the <ns0:hi>General Resurrection</ns0:hi> (to which all shall come worthy, or unworthy) but of the <ns0:hi>Resurrection unto Life.</ns0:hi> That Resurrection which is not the meer effect of Divine Providence, necessary in order to the last Judgment, but that <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi> to Life, which is the <ns0:hi>Effect of Christs purchase.</ns0:hi> And this is observable, that the <ns0:hi>Resurrection from the Dead,</ns0:hi> will be of so little advantage; nay of such miserable disadvantage to wicked Men, that the Scripture sometimes speaketh of the Resurrection, as if it were peculiar to Saints. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.22. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 3.11. So in this Text, hence <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> calls them afterward, the <ns0:hi>Children of the Resurrection</ns0:hi>; not that others shall not rise, but the <ns0:hi>Children of God</ns0:hi> alone shall be the Favourites of the Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection; those who shall rise as Children to an Eternal In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />heritance. Concerning the state of Persons in the <ns0:hi>Resurrection,</ns0:hi> our Saviour thus describes it: That Men and Women there shall be <ns0:hi>as the Angels,</ns0:hi> not in all things, but in the things mentioned, which are two, One of them mentioned by <ns0:hi>Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew,</ns0:hi> both by <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> 1. <ns0:hi>They shall not dye any more.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>They shall not Marry, nor be give in Marriage.</ns0:hi> The first shew<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth the needlessness of the latter; for one great reason of Marriage, was to supply the Gaps which Death maketh in the World; but Men shall not dye any more, therefore there will be no need of Conjugal Relations amongst Men, more than among Angels. <ns0:hi>The Children of this World</ns0:hi> (saith <ns0:hi>Luke) Marry, and are given in Marriage. Marriage</ns0:hi> was only an institution for this World, and is to continue no longer than this World stands; for the state of Men in another World, will be such as needs it not, being a state of <ns0:hi>Immortality,</ns0:hi> so not needing it for Propagation: And a <ns0:hi>state for Perfection,</ns0:hi> and so not needing it for mutual help in the Affairs of Mans Life, nor a Remedy against extravagant Lust.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 3.12. Act. 7.32. Heb. 11.16.</ns0:note> I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And when the multitude heard <ns0:hi>this,</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> they were astonished at his doctrine.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.26, 27. So hath <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 20.37, 38. only <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> mention the time when God spake these Words.—<ns0:hi>In the Bush,</ns0:hi> that is, when God appeared to <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>burning Bush. Exod.</ns0:hi> 3.6. and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>for all Live unto him. Mark</ns0:hi> also saith, <ns0:hi>Concerning the Dead that they Rise, have you not read in the Book of Moses</ns0:hi>? Our Saviour in the foregoing Words, had by the by asserted the Doctrine of <ns0:hi>Angels,</ns0:hi> here he asserts both <ns0:hi>the Doctrine of the Immortality of the Soul,</ns0:hi> and also of the Resurrection of the Body; and tho <ns0:hi>Cardinal Perron,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Maldonate the Iesuite</ns0:hi> boldly assert, that the Resurrection of the Body cannot be proved from hence, without taking in the Tradition of the Church; yet, notwithstanding their Confidence, those who have a greater Reverence for our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour's Words, think that not only the <ns0:hi>Immortality of the Soul,</ns0:hi> but the <ns0:hi>Resurrection of the Body</ns0:hi> also, is irrefrag<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>bly proved by this Argument of our Saviours; to make out which, these things are to be observed, 1. God doth not say I <ns0:hi>have been,</ns0:hi> but I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi>: He speaketh of the time present, when he spake to <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> and of the <ns0:hi>time to come.</ns0:hi> 2. He doth not say, I <ns0:hi>am the Lord of Abraham, Isaac,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> But the <ns0:hi>God of</ns0:hi>: Now wherever God stiles himself the <ns0:hi>God of any People,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Person,</ns0:hi> it always signifieth, <ns0:hi>God as a Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nefactor,</ns0:hi> and one that doth, and will do good to such a People, or Person. It is a foederal Expression, as where he saith to <ns0:hi>Abraham, Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.7. <ns0:hi>I will be a God to thee and thy Seed, that is, of thee, and of thy Seed.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob, doth not signifie part of Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob, but their entire Persons,</ns0:hi> which consist of Bodies as well as Souls. 4. <ns0:hi>God is not the God of the Dead,</ns0:hi> he doth not shew kindness to them if they be Dead, and shall Rise no more. 5. In this Life, <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob,</ns0:hi> received no such signal kindness from God, but others might receive as great kindness, as any of them did. Hence now our Lord proveth as the Immortality of their Souls, so the Resurrection also of their Bodies, that God might shew him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self the God of whole <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob. Gerard</ns0:hi> saith, The Argument of this Text is made clear, by <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 11.16. <ns0:hi>Wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he hath prepared for them a City.</ns0:hi> This is that which made God, to be truly called <ns0:hi>their God</ns0:hi>; because he <ns0:hi>hath prepared for them a City,</ns0:hi> which City they could never possess without a <ns0:hi>Resurrection.</ns0:hi> It is yet further added by some, That Gods promise to <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> of the Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> was in these terms, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 13.15. <ns0:hi>To thee will I give it, and thy Seed for ever:</ns0:hi> Not only to <ns0:hi>thy Seed,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>to thee</ns0:hi>; so to <ns0:hi>Isa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>c, Gen.</ns0:hi> 26.3. To <ns0:hi>Iacob, Gen</ns0:hi> 35.12. <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 6.4.8. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 11.21. The Promises seemed not to be fulfilled, in giving their Posterity the Earthly <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> which <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob</ns0:hi> lived not to enjoy, but to extend, to the <ns0:hi>Rest</ns0:hi> prepared for the People of God, the <ns0:hi>City</ns0:hi> mentioned by the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 11.16. which God had prepared for them, to justifie himself to be <ns0:hi>their God.</ns0:hi> Now this could not be pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pared for their <ns0:hi>Souls</ns0:hi> meerly, which were but a part of them, and hardly capable of perfect Happiness, without a Re-union with the Body, there being in it such an innate Desire. Nor was it reasonable, that the Bodies of these Saints having been sharers with their Souls in their Labours, should have no share in their reward from that Covenant; therefore of God with <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob,</ns0:hi> our Saviour firmly proveth their Resurrection. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>For all live unto him.</ns0:hi> Not live unto him only as their End. But in the same Sense, as <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 6.10. of Christ. <ns0:hi>In that he liveth, he liveth unto God:</ns0:hi> That is, with God. So saith <ns0:hi>Luke, Abra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ham, Isaac,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> tho Dead at present, live with God, and they, and all the Children of <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> shall live to God, that is, with God to all Eternity. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>When the multitudes heard this, they were astonished at his Do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctrine.</ns0:hi> Poor People, they had been used to hear Discourses from the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> about the <ns0:hi>Traditions of the Elders, Rites,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ceremonies, washing Hands before Meat,</ns0:hi> and the nece<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ssity of <ns0:hi>washing Pots,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cups,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Sadduces</ns0:hi> declaiming against the Doctrines of <ns0:hi>Angels</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Spirits,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection,</ns0:hi> they were astonished to hear one instructing them in things concerned their Souls, the <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Life Eternal,</ns0:hi> and Confuting their great Teachers, from Books of Scripture owned by themselves; for the <ns0:hi>Sadduces,</ns0:hi> tho they had no great regard to the Prophets, yet they owned, and payed a great deference to the Books of <ns0:hi>Moses.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadduces to silence, they were gather<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed together.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 Then one of them <ns0:hi>which was</ns0:hi> a lawyer, ask<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> a qustion, tempting him, and saying,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:260" />36 Master! which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the great commandement in the law?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 Jesus said unto him, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 10.12. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 30.6.</ns0:note> Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 This is the first, and great commande<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And the second <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> like unto it, <ns0:note place="margin">Lev. 19.18. Rom. 13.9. Gal. 5.14. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 2.8.</ns0:note> Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thy self.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 7.12.</ns0:note> On these two commandements, hang all the law, and the prophets.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> relateth this History more fully, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34. <ns0:hi>And one of the Scribes came, and having heard them reasoning together, and perceiving that he had answered them well, asked him, which is the first Comman<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dement of all? And Iesus answered him, the first of all the Commandments is, hear O Israel, the Lord thy God is one Lord. And thou shalt love the Lord thy God, with all thy Heart, and with all thy Soul, and with all thy Mind, and with all thy Strength. This is the first Commandement. And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy Neighbour as thy self; there is no other Commandement great<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er than these, And the Scribe said unto him, Well Master thou hast said the Truth, for there is one God, and there is none other but he. And to love him with all the Heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the Soul, and with all the Strength, and to love his Neighbour as himself, is more than all whole Burnt Offerings and Sacrifices. And when Iesus saw that he answered Discreetly, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the Kingdom of God. And no Man after that, durst ask him any Question. Luke</ns0:hi> omitteth this Hi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ory, only subjoyneth to our Saviours An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swer to the <ns0:hi>Sadduces, Ch.</ns0:hi> 20. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 39, 40. <ns0:hi>Then certain o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> the Scribes Answering, said, Master thou hast well said. And after that they durst not ask him any Q<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>estion at all.</ns0:hi> There are different Opinions of Interpreters, concerning the De<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sign of this <ns0:hi>Scribe,</ns0:hi> called by <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Lawyer,</ns0:hi> in coming to Christ with this Question<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Some think that he came up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on the same Errand with the others, to entangle him in his Speech. Others, that he came meerly out of a desire to be more fully instructed by him, and that <ns0:hi>Tempting</ns0:hi> here, signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fies no more than <ns0:hi>Trying him,</ns0:hi> not for a bad end, but as the <ns0:hi>Queen</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Sheba</ns0:hi> came to prove <ns0:hi>Solomon with hard Questions,</ns0:hi> to have an Experiment of his Wisdom. Our Saviours fair Treat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLunhyphen" />ing him, and the Commendation he gave him, together with his fair speaking to our Saviour, and Commending his Answer induce me, to think that he came on no ill Design. Besides, that the Opinion of some, that he came hoping to hear our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />our vilify their <ns0:hi>Ritual Precepts,</ns0:hi> in Comparison of the <ns0:hi>Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral Precepts,</ns0:hi> seemeth to me not probable, for himself con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLunhyphen" />sents to what our Saviour saith, and addeth, that <ns0:hi>To love the Lord our God,</ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>is more than all Burnt Offerings and Sacrifices.</ns0:hi> His Question was, <ns0:hi>Which is the first and great<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est Commandement? Matthew</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>the great; Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>The first:</ns0:hi> they have both the same Sense, and our Saviour <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 38. puts them together. <ns0:hi>Iesus saith unto him, thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy Heart, and with all thy Soul, and with all thy Mind. Mark</ns0:hi> adds, <ns0:hi>with all thy Strength.</ns0:hi> It is to be found, <ns0:hi>Deut,</ns0:hi> 6.5. only there is not <ns0:hi>with all thy Mind. Luke</ns0:hi> puts it in, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.27. It is but the same thing expressed in Diverse Terms, for <ns0:hi>with all thy Soul,</ns0:hi> is Comprehensive of <ns0:hi>Heart, Mind,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Strength. Mark</ns0:hi> adds a Preface. <ns0:hi>Hear O Israel, the Lord thy God is one God, Thou shalt love,</ns0:hi> &c. those words, only 1. stirred up the Peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples Attention. 2. Shewed the reason of the following pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cept, which is fully expressed in <ns0:hi>Matthew.</ns0:hi> If any ask, to which of the Ten Commandements is this to be referred? It is easily answered, that it is the Sum of the four first, which Comprehend our Duty toward God. Our Saviours expres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing them by <ns0:hi>loving God,</ns0:hi> shews us that the Law of God was not fulfilled, in the Observation of the Letter of those Comman<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dements, but doing these things which God Commands out of a Principle of <ns0:hi>Love,</ns0:hi> the highest Degrees of Love to God. They idly Interpret this Precept, who Interpret it only an Obligation upon us, to <ns0:hi>Love God</ns0:hi> as much as we are able in our Lapsed State, the <ns0:hi>fall of Man</ns0:hi> lost God no right of Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manding, and telling us our Duty. The Law doth undoub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tedly require of us <ns0:hi>Love to God</ns0:hi> in the highest Degree, to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> shewed by the Acts of the whole Man, in obedience to all his Commandments, and that constantly. It is our only Hap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />piness that the Law is in the Hands of a Mediator, who hath thus perfectly fulfilled it, for all those who believe in him, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.3. and accepteth of us, the Will, for the Deed. Thus the Moral Law is a Scool-Master that leadeth us unto Christ. Our Saviour justly calls this the first and great Commandment. 1. Because God is to be served before our Neighbour. 2. Nor can love to our Neighbour flow from any other true Principle, than that of Love to God, nor is our Neighbour to be loved, but for Gods sake, and in Subordination unto him. <ns0:hi>And the second is like to it.</ns0:hi> Commanding <ns0:hi>Love</ns0:hi> also; So that as the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle saith, <ns0:hi>Love is the fulfilling of the Law.</ns0:hi> [thy Neigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bour] that is, every Man, <ns0:hi>as thy self,</ns0:hi> doing as much for him as thou wouldst have him do for thee, and doing no more a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst him, than thou wouldst willingly he should do against thee. As truly and sincerely, as thy self. <ns0:hi>On these two Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mandements hang all the Law and the Prophets.</ns0:hi> There is nothing commanded in all the Old Testament but may be reduced to these two Heads. This is the whole Duty of Man there commanded. The whole Book of God is our Rule, and we are obliged to every Precept in it. <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> summed up all in the Ten Commandements, to which truly interpreted all the precepts of Scripture are reducible, Christ here brings the Ten to Two. The Apostle brings all to one, telling us <ns0:hi>Love is the fulfilling of the Law.</ns0:hi> There is nothing forbidden in Scripture, but what offends the <ns0:hi>Royal Law or Love,</ns0:hi> either to God or Man: There is nothing commanded, but what will fall under it. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> addeth, that the <ns0:hi>Scribe</ns0:hi> applauds our Saviour, as having said <ns0:hi>the Truth,</ns0:hi> and Confe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sing, that the fulfilling these two Precepts, was <ns0:hi>more than all Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fices and burnt Offerings,</ns0:hi> in which he agreed with <ns0:hi>Samuel,</ns0:hi> who long since told <ns0:hi>Saul,</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>to obey was better than Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice,</ns0:hi> and it needs must be so, seeing that all the true value of Sacrifices, lay in the <ns0:hi>Obedience,</ns0:hi> by them given to the Will of God. Christ tells the <ns0:hi>Scribe, He was not far from the Kingdom of God.</ns0:hi> He who once rightly understands the Law of God, and hath cast off that silly fancy or thinking to please God with Ritual things, hath made a great Proficiency un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der that School-Ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>er, who if rightly under<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ood, will shew him the need of another Righteo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sness than his own, wherein to appear before God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 While the Pharisees were gathered toge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, Jesus asked them,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 Saying, What think ye of Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, <ns0:hi>The son</ns0:hi> of David.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 He saith untothem, How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 15.25. Heb. 1.13, <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.12, 13.</ns0:note> The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, 'till I make thine enemies thy foot stool.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 And no man was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth, ask him any more questions.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath this Story, shortly repeating only the substance of it, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.35, 36, 37. adding nothing to it, but con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cluding. <ns0:hi>And the common People heard him g<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>adly. Luke</ns0:hi> repeateth it as shortly, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 20.41, 42, 43<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> For the right understanding of this Discourse of our Saviour to the <ns0:hi>Phari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sees,</ns0:hi> we must know, that tho the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> and the Jews in general<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> did expect a <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> or a Christ, yet they expected no more of him, or in him, than that he should be <ns0:hi>a Man,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> descended from his Family according to the promise, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 9.6. and dreamed only of a <ns0:hi>Secular Prince,</ns0:hi> who should deliver them from their Enemies, and re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />store them to their Ancient Civil Liberties. Christ seeing a pack of them together, took the Liberty, which he had al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed them towards himself, to propo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>nd a Question or two to them. His question was. <ns0:hi>What they thought of Christ?</ns0:hi> Not of himself but of the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> whom they expected? whose Son he should be? they say unto him, <ns0:hi>The Son of Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid,</ns0:hi> that is, one who should in a right Line be descended from <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi> This was a constant, and uncontrouled Tra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition amongst them. Hence <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, the <ns0:hi>Question</ns0:hi> was pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pounded, <ns0:hi>How say the Scribes? Luke, how say they,</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> is, that is, is to be the <ns0:hi>Son of David</ns0:hi>! This was a com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon received Opinion amongst them, which our Saviour by the next Words doth not contradict, but only argueth that he must needs be something more: for (saith he) <ns0:hi>How then doth</ns0:hi> David <ns0:hi>in Spirit call him Lord? Psal.</ns0:hi> 110, 1. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>David himself said by the Holy Ghost. David</ns0:hi> was a <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> and spake by inspiration from the Holy Ghost. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.16. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 2.30. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>in the Psalms,</ns0:hi> whence we may observe, that <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 110. was <ns0:hi>Davids</ns0:hi> Psalm, not a <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> composed by some other for <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> as some contend, would <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> have called him <ns0:hi>Lord,</ns0:hi> whom he knew to be meerly his Son, one that should only descend from him? He would have said, <ns0:hi>The Lord said to my Son,</ns0:hi> or will say to my Son. <ns0:hi>The Lord said, Iehovah</ns0:hi> said <ns0:hi>to my Lord: Sit thou on my right Hand.</ns0:hi> Would <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> speaking Prophetically by the Holy Ghost concerning the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> had he believed he was to be his Son, and no more, have said, that <ns0:hi>Iehovah</ns0:hi> should say unto him, <ns0:hi>sit on my Right Hand,</ns0:hi> a place of the highest Honour, Dignity, and Favour, <ns0:hi>untill I make thy Enemies thy Footstool,</ns0:hi> that is, for ever, for <ns0:hi>un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />til</ns0:hi> doth not signifie a Determinate time. See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 1.25. <ns0:hi>If David then call him Lord! How is he then his Son.</ns0:hi> That is, how is he then no more than his Son, no more than a meer Man: Our Saviour by this Argument doth neither go about to prove, that <ns0:hi>the Christ</ns0:hi> was not to be the Son of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> nor that he was the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> himself, but that their expected <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> or Christ, must be more than a meer man, otherwise <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> would never have called him <ns0:hi>Lord,</ns0:hi> nor yet Prophesied, th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t <ns0:hi>Iehovah</ns0:hi> should call him to <ns0:hi>Sit at his Right Hand. Matthew</ns0:hi> concludes with telling us, that as the <ns0:hi>Sad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duces</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> were Non plust before; so now the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> Mouths were also stopped. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, the <ns0:hi>Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon People heard him gladly. Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>No Man was able to answer him a Word, neither durst any man ask him an<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> more questions.</ns0:hi> Nor shall we hear of their troubling him with disputes any more, they now see Disputing will not do their business, their next Business is to consult how to take away his Life, which is always the Course of <ns0:hi>Proud,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />licious Men,</ns0:hi> given over of God to ruin, to conceal their Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />victions, and proceed to Execute their Lusts and Malice, ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther than they will not have their Ends. But before they meet with a fit opportunity, we shall have some excellent Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />courses from our Saviour, to the Disciples, and the Multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
